newsitem.title: NORWAY: Price pressure on contrast media hits Nycomed Q1.
newsitem.headline: Price pressure on contrast media hits Nycomed Q1.

text.p: Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Nycomed ASA said on Tuesday that pressure on prices for its diagnostic contrast media and lower contract production were responsible for a seven percent dip in operating revenues in the first quarter.
The company posted operating revenues of 1.84 billion crowns against 1.99 billion crowns in the year-ago period.

Profits before tax amounted to 271 million crowns, a slump of 33 percent from 402 million crowns, while operating profits after research and development costs (R&D) totalled 304 million crowns versus 442 million crowns.
"The price decline on contrast media was partially offset by higher sales volumes," Nycomed said in a statement.

Operating revenues for the group's medical imaging business declined 13 percent to 1.07 billion crowns and operating profits slipped 31 percent to 384 million crowns against 553 million crowns in the first quarter 1996.
The operating margin before R&D costs was almost two percent lower than the fourth quarter last year.
Nycomed said prices of X-ray contrast media in the United States fell by over 30 percent in the first three months compared with a year ago.
"The prices stabilised toward the end of 1996 and there have been only minor changes in the first quarter 1997," the company's statement said.
"Markets outside of the USA also experienced negative price developments in 1996, although the price fall was more moderate."
In the therapeutics sector operating revenues increased two percent to 779 million crowns from 766 million crowns, while operating profit before R&D was 130 million crowns versus 114 million crowns.

Nycomed attributed the rise in revenues largely to higher export sales to Japan and other markets despite the adverse impact of a strong Norwegian crown. Sales in the Nordic and some other European markets were on par with 1996.
The improvement in operating profit was primarily due to a better product mix, it said.
The company said its Focus '98 cost-reduction programme was proceeding as planned, including the shutdown of all research activities in Austria.

"As a result of the Austrian restructuring and an adjustment of the R&D activity in medical imaging, R&D costs in the ensuing quarters are expected to be commensurate with the first quarter," the statement said.
First-quarter R&D costs amounted to 189 million crowns, corresponding to 10 percent of operating revenues.
